title: Memory Allocators in C
summary: Build allocators from nothing: alignment, bump arenas, fixed-size pools, a splitting and coalescing free-list heap, fit policies and a fragmentation map.
description: malloc is not magic: it is bookkeeping over a block of memory. In this course you work on a static buffer and write the pieces yourself. You start with alignment arithmetic, then a bump arena with reset and rewind, a fixed-size pool with an in-place free list, and a general heap with block headers, splitting and coalescing. You compare first-fit and best-fit with deterministic counters, draw the heap as an ASCII fragmentation map, and finish by combining pools and the heap into a size-class allocator. Hidden tests replay seeded random operation sequences against an independent reference model and check invariants: no overlap, alignment, contents preserved, full coalescing and bounded overhead. These are teaching allocators on a single thread; the kernel heap lessons in the osdev tracks cover the same ideas on bare metal, so here the focus is the algorithms and how to test them.
outcomes: Compute aligned addresses and struct layouts without overflow.
Write a bump arena, a fixed-size pool and a splitting, coalescing free-list heap.
Compare allocation policies with deterministic counters and read a fragmentation map.
Test an allocator against a reference model with seeded random operation sequences.
